title: Forgejo and Codeberg
description: "Use Codeberg and self-hosted Forgejo instances: issues, pull requests, notifications, releases and webhooks."
icon: i-simple-icons-forgejo

The Forgejo provider covers Codeberg and self-hosted Forgejo instances. It reads and writes issues and pull requests. It also covers notifications, commit statuses, releases, repository contents and repository and organisation webhooks. The [Gitea](/providers/gitea) provider uses the same implementation.

## Authentication

The provider accepts an access token. OAuth2 applications on Forgejo issue user tokens, which you pass the same way:

```ts
import { forgejo } from 'forges/forgejo'

const forge = forgejo({
  auth: { type: 'token', token: process.env.CODEBERG_TOKEN! },
}).create()
```

Without `auth`, the provider makes anonymous public reads.

## Instance

The default instance is `https://codeberg.org`. For a self-hosted instance, set `baseUrl` to the root of the instance. The provider appends `/api/v1`:

```ts
forgejo({ baseUrl: 'https://git.example.com', auth })
```

`refreshCapabilities()` reads the instance version from `/version`.

## Marking notifications done

Forgejo notifications have a read state but no done state. `markDone()` is `'emulated'`: it marks the notification read and unsubscribes from the thread.

## Merging

If you don't pass `method`, `merge()` reads the merge styles that the repository allows. When exactly one style is allowed, it uses that style. When several are allowed, it throws `MergeMethodRequiredError`. With `whenChecksPass`, Forgejo merges the pull request after its checks succeed.

## Reviews

Reviews are native. `createReview()` without an `event` creates a pending review, and `submitReview()` submits it. The API doesn't expose whether a review conversation is resolved, so `resolveReviewThread()` is unavailable.

## Checks and CI

`checks.list()` reads commit statuses, and `checks.report()` writes them. Forgejo Actions has no stable API for runs and jobs, so `checks.rerun()` and the `ci` methods are unavailable.

## Changed files

`threads.files()` and `contents.compare()` return line counts for each file, but no `patch`. Forgejo serves diffs only for a whole pull request.

## Search

`search.threads()` searches across repositories. It has no `involves` filter and returns results newest first. Passing `involves` adds a `filter_unsupported` warning. Passing a `sort` other than `relevance` adds a `sort_unsupported` warning.

## Webhooks

Set `webhookSecret` to the secret configured on the hook:

```ts
const forge = forgejo({
  webhookSecret: process.env.FORGEJO_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
}).create()

const events = await forge.webhooks.ingest({
  headers: request.headers,
  body: await request.text(),
})
```

Forgejo sends these headers with each delivery:

| Header | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Forgejo-Signature` | The hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body |
| `X-Forgejo-Event` | The event name |
| `X-Forgejo-Delivery` | The delivery ID |

The provider also accepts the `X-Gitea-*` version of each header.

A label delivery doesn't say which labels were added or removed. A changed label set becomes a `label` event with the `edited` action, and removing every label becomes one with the `unlabelled` action.

`webhooks.deliveries()` and `webhooks.redeliver()` are unavailable.

::contributing{title="Record Forgejo fixtures" to="/contributing/record-fixtures"}
```sh
CODEBERG_TOKEN=... FIXTURE_FORGEJO_REPO=owner/repo \
FIXTURE_FORGEJO_PULL=1 pnpm record-fixtures forgejo
```

To add an issue, set `FIXTURE_FORGEJO_ISSUE`. To record another instance, set `CODEBERG_BASE_URL`.
::
